Three small self-test tasks: using public information and fictional site conditions, write a scheme description for a small building (functional and spatial requirements, form and circulation, the code basis to be adopted, and the main technical trade-offs); use fictional drawings to make one code compliance checklist (fire compartments and evacuation, storey height and clear height, accessibility and daylight and ventilation, and so on, with conclusions); and write one multi-disciplinary coordination meeting as 500-character minutes (the items raised by each discipline, the points of conflict, the proposed solutions and the items to be confirmed). (Editorial suggestion, not recruitment, a qualification examination or a skills test, and it does not describe the process of any design institution.)

People who are more likely to adapt: those willing to do detailed work on drawings and technical documents over the long term and to review them repeatedly (48% consider precision or accuracy extremely important and 39% very important; 22% consider the consequences of error very serious, 35% serious and 26% somewhat serious), those able to move projects forward in multi-disciplinary coordination and client communication (70% consider teamwork extremely important and 22% very important; 61% have face-to-face discussions every day, 83% have telephone conversations every day and 100% use email every day), those able to accept a longer working week and a regular fixed schedule (57% work more than 40 hours per week and 78% have a regular fixed schedule), and those able to stop, record and escalate when problems are found, in line with the codes and the scope of practice. Risk is usually greater if the person finds repeated drawing revisions and multi-party coordination hard to accept, is uncomfortable with construction site observation and travel, is unwilling to record and review according to the codes, or lacks awareness of the boundaries of the scope of practice and sealing responsibility.

In one sentence: a professional post that starts from building functional and spatial requirements and, through scheme design, preparation of drawings and technical specifications, specialist integration and code checking, and construction coordination and site observation, delivers architectural design outputs (schemes, construction drawings, technical specifications and design documents) that are buildable, reviewable and traceable.

The work of architects can be divided into four categories: scheme design and drawing presentation (communicating with clients to establish functional and spatial requirements, preparing scale drawings and architectural schemes, producing three-dimensional or interactive presentations, and planning floor layouts and circulation); specialist integration and code checking (integrating engineering elements such as structure, plumbing, heating and electrical systems and fire protection into a unified design, supervising the work of specialist consultants, and checking the design against codes on environment and safety and calculating energy-saving potential); construction drawings and contract documents (preparing the final construction drawings and construction contract documents, compiling information on design structure, materials, colours, equipment, estimates and programme, and preparing operation and maintenance manuals or research reports); and construction coordination and business (visiting sites regularly to observe whether construction matches the drawings, administering construction contracts, tendering or awarding contracts on behalf of the client, and preparing proposals and presentations to win new business).

O*NET 17-1011.00 Architect (Architects, Except Landscape and Naval): plan and design buildings such as private residences, office buildings, theatres, factories and other structural properties. The common job titles listed on the page include architect, architectural designer, design architect, planner, project architect and specification writer. The interest code is RCA (Realistic, Conventional, Artistic); the page lists 25 tasks. This occupation requires extensive preparation (Job Zone Five, SVP 8.0 and above), and among the respondent answers 43% consider a master's degree necessary, 39% a bachelor's degree and 13% a post-bachelor certificate. All 25 tasks are core tasks; 43/39/13 are responses about the education needed for new entrants, not the education composition of existing practitioners or a Chinese statutory threshold.

entries: Scheme design and drawing presentation | Turn requirements into verifiable design outputs | Communicate functional and spatial requirements with clients, plan floor layouts and circulation, prepare scale drawings and architectural schemes, and produce three-dimensional or interactive presentations using computer-aided design software.

Specialist integration and code checking | Make the design stand up technically and legally | Integrate engineering elements such as structure, plumbing, heating and electrical systems and fire protection into a unified design, supervise the work of specialist consultants, and check the design against codes on environment and safety and assess compliance.

Preparation of construction drawings and contract documents | Produce documents usable for construction and review | Prepare final construction drawings covering aesthetic presentation and construction details, compile information on structure, materials, colours, equipment, estimates and programme, and prepare construction contract documents and operation and maintenance manuals.

Construction coordination and site observation | Make the design land during construction | Visit sites regularly to observe whether construction matches the drawings, administer construction contracts, tender or award construction contracts on behalf of the client, and handle clarifications and changes during the construction stage.

Green building and existing building upgrading | Put sustainability requirements into the design | Design or plan projects to green building standards, design environmentally friendly upgrading of existing buildings (natural daylight, green roofs, rainwater collection and so on), and calculate energy-saving potential by comparing design energy consumption with a baseline standard.

Preliminary services and business development | Take a project from feasible to winnable | Carry out preliminary services such as feasibility or environmental impact work, collect information on a project's environmental sustainability and operational efficiency, and prepare marketing material, proposals and presentations to win new business.

Boundaries come down to four things: who bears design responsibility and sealing, who bears construction and safety responsibility, who approves planning, construction drawings and fire protection, and who determines cost and programme. Within the commission, architects complete the scheme, the construction drawings, specialist integration and code checking and seal the design documents; construction quality and site safety are the responsibility of the construction unit; planning permission and construction drawing review and fire design review are the responsibility of the competent authorities and the review bodies established by law; cost and programme are governed by the contract and require client confirmation. The design output is a professional document and does not replace administrative approval or the general contracting responsibility for construction; where the scope of practice and conflicts of interest are involved, the Regulations and institutional rules apply.
Complete the design, specialist integration and code checking within the commission.

Answer design delivery questions with: whether the use, functional requirements and code basis are stated; whether the drawings, calculations and review records can be checked; whether the specialist integration conditions are closed; whether design changes are traceable; and whether the output is issued within the scope of practice and sealing requirements.

Do not count adjacent responsibilities (construction organisation and site safety of the construction unit, quality and schedule monitoring of the supervision unit, specialist design and calculation by structural and plumbing, heating and electrical professional engineers, interior space and furnishing by interior designers, outdoor site and landscape by landscape architects, plan preparation and land use policy by urban and regional planners, and bills of quantities and pricing by cost engineers) as core tasks of this occupation.

The objects are the function, space, form and technical conditions of buildings; the basis is architectural design and detailing principles, engineering construction standards on fire protection, evacuation, accessibility and energy efficiency, green building assessment standards, client functional, budget and programme requirements, and regulations such as the Construction Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on Registered Architects of the People's Republic of China and their registered practice requirements.

Architects plan and design buildings such as housing, office buildings, theatres and factories; the core is analysing requirements and the site, expressing the scheme, integrating engineering disciplines, checking the codes, construction drawings and contract documents, site observation and handling changes. Green building and existing building upgrading are also within the O*NET task scope. A registered architect must register with a unit that holds an engineering design qualification, and the unit accepts commissions and charges uniformly; first class practice is not limited by project scale or complexity, second class practice is limited to stipulated small projects, and the individual scope is also subject to the unit's business scope. Architectural schemes and presentation drawings, construction drawings, technical specifications and material and equipment schedules, specialist integration records for structure and plumbing, heating and electrical systems, calculation books and code checking tables, construction contract documents and estimate and programme notes, site observation and design change records, and review records and design documents and sealed archive material.

Responsibility is divided according to the commission and the registered practice requirements; before starting, check the institution's qualification and business scope, whether the person has obtained registered architect qualification and the registration scope (first class is not limited by scale or complexity while second class is limited to small-scale projects stipulated by the state), whether practising in one's own name is permitted, the sealing and review process for design documents, safety arrangements for site observation and travel, and the confidentiality and archive retention requirements for drawings, models and client requirements.

The scheme, construction drawings and design responsibility are borne by the architect and the design unit; construction organisation and site safety are the responsibility of the construction unit; quality and schedule monitoring are the responsibility of the supervision unit; specialist design for structure and plumbing, heating and electrical systems is the responsibility of the corresponding professional engineers; interior, landscape, planning and cost work is borne by interior designers, landscape architects, urban and regional planners and cost engineers respectively; and planning permission and construction drawing and fire design review are the responsibility of the competent authorities and the review bodies.

In mainland China, a distinction must be drawn between design support posts and registered practice: an unregistered person may assist with drafting, document organisation and design in a design unit under the guidance and review of the person in charge, but must not practise in the name of a registered architect or sign on their behalf. A registered architect must register with a unit that holds an engineering design qualification, and the unit accepts commissions and charges uniformly; first class practice is not limited by project scale or complexity, second class practice is limited to stipulated small projects, and the individual scope is also subject to the unit's business scope. The main design documents for projects of the stipulated scale must be signed and sealed by the registered architect in charge of the design. Every US state and the District of Columbia requires architects to be licensed, usually through architectural education, supervised paid internship and a qualification examination; the internship is generally about 3 years and some student experience may count towards it. The related work experience of none in the BLS entry-level table does not exempt a person from the licensing internship. The O*NET education responses of 43% master's, 39% bachelor's and 13% post-bachelor certificate are a respondent distribution and cannot replace state statutory requirements. Subject pass validity and registration validity differ: 8 years for first class and 4 years for second class, with a registration period of 2 years.

Design practice must follow the regulations and technical standards: drawings, calculation books, review records and seals must not be forged or tampered with, and business must not be conducted in the name of a registered architect beyond the scope of practice; design quality must be assured and the drawings one is responsible for must be signed, secrets of units and individuals learned in practice must be kept, a person must not simultaneously be employed by two or more architectural design units to conduct business, and others must not be permitted to conduct business in one's own name; client, project, cost and tender material must be handled in line with confidentiality and personal information protection requirements.

When site conditions do not match the data, specialist conditions conflict, code compliance is in doubt, the cost or programme premise does not hold, client requirements exceed the scope of practice or an undisclosed conflict of interest exists, the relevant design work should be paused, the data corrected or the limitations stated truthfully, and the matter reported through institutional and technical review procedures; untrue or unreviewed design documents must not be issued because of schedule or tender pressure.

Design outputs apply only to a specific use, site condition, code version and design stage; the same building may be built differently under a different scheme or different cost and functional conditions, the construction drawings are governed by the version that has been reviewed and sealed, drawings from the scheme stage or renderings must not be treated as a basis for construction, and drawings that have not been reviewed must not be used for permit application or construction.

Before starting, check at least six items: work direction (public buildings and scheme design, housing and standardised design, construction drawings and technical development, existing building upgrading and green building, and so on); qualification and scope of practice (whether the registered architect examination has been passed and registration obtained, first or second class scope of practice, the institution's qualification and business scope, and whether signing and sealing design documents is permitted); working method and intensity (repeated drawing revisions and multi-disciplinary coordination, the working week and schedule (57% more than 40 hours, 78% regular and fixed) and site observation and travel arrangements); records and compliance requirements (drawing and model versions and review traceability, sealing and scope of practice control, and confidentiality of client and project data); employment and income method (full-time in a design institution, client-side design management, consulting and advisory work, project-based or monthly, and whether project bonuses are included); and development path (deepening a specialist direction, obtaining first class registered architect status and leading large projects, moving into design management or switching to planning and green building and design management directions).
Look at the work direction and the nature of the institution, not the job title.

Work directions: public buildings and scheme design, housing and standardised design, construction drawings and technical development, existing building upgrading and green building, design management and client-side design management, and urban design and architectural pre-scheme planning; different directions differ in project types, code emphasis, output form and clients.
Practice qualification and registration scope determine whether one can conduct business and sign design documents in the name of a registered architect.

Qualification and scope of practice: whether the national first or second class registered architect qualification examination has been passed and registration obtained, whether the registration is still valid, the first or second class scope of practice (second class must not exceed the building scale and engineering complexity stipulated by the state), whether the institution's qualification and business scope cover the project type, whether content requiring specialist review such as fire protection and structure is involved, and whether continuing education must be completed on an ongoing basis.
The working method, intensity and traceability requirements directly affect whether the work can be done compliantly and sustainably.

Working and compliance conditions: long hours at a desk and eye strain caused by repeated drawing revisions and multi-disciplinary integration, the working week and schedule regularity, and site observation and travel arrangements; standards for drawing and model versions and review traceability, sealing and scope of practice control, confidentiality requirements for client requirements and cost and tender material, and archive retention requirements for design documents and calculation books.
The nature of the institution and the project cycle affect long-term sustainability.

Employment and income method: stability and protection differ between full-time work in a design institution, client-side design management and consulting or advisory work; 57% work more than 40 hours per week and 78% have a regular fixed schedule, and income is affected by project sources, construction investment and tender competition, so it must be checked against the actual contract and project arrangements.
Specialist accumulation, scope of practice and project records support development; a degree or qualification alone cannot guarantee promotion.

Development path: whether stable specialist capability can be built in one direction (public buildings, housing, construction drawings and technical development, existing building upgrading and green building), whether first class registered architect status can be obtained through the examination and large or complex projects led, whether the person can move into a design management and technical lead post, or switch to urban design and architectural planning, green building and energy consulting, or client-side design management and construction management.
Check the official and institutional requirements first, then decide on the investment.

paragraphs: Suggested order of choices: first decide the direction (public buildings and scheme design, housing and standardised design, or construction drawings and technical development), then check the practice qualification and the institution's business scope (whether the national first and second class registered architect examination has been passed and registration obtained, first or second class scope of practice, and whether the institution's qualification covers the project type and scale), and finally confirm the working method and intensity, the drawing and sealing traceability requirements, the employment and income method and the development path. All directions share functional and spatial judgement, drawing presentation, specialist integration and code checking ability; moving to an adjacent occupation requires building up different abilities and qualifications (structural and load calculation, construction organisation and site management and cost and programme, interior space and materials and furnishing, site and municipal and landscape engineering, land use and transport and policy analysis, building services and engineering economics), and the responsibility systems differ, so it cannot be transferred directly.

The comparison is based on the O*NET architect tasks, the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook, the 2026 amended Regulations on Registered Architects and the detailed rules, and the 2022 related sub-category of building and municipal design engineering technicians. Adjacent responsibilities and transitions are an editorial comparison, and qualifications cannot be transferred.

Projects are mostly public buildings and large complexes; the focus is form and circulation and public space quality and client communication, and there are many code and review steps and frequent scheme revisions.

Projects are mostly housing and standardised, high-volume construction; the focus is unit planning, codes, cost control and drafting efficiency, with high demands on standardisation and repeated checking.

Complete standardised design to product and unit-plan requirements and prepare generic methods and nodes, control methods and materials to meet cost and permit application requirements, and produce and check drawings in batches.

Projects are mainly construction drawings and technical development; the focus is specialist integration, construction nodes, code compliance and drawing quality, and this is the key stage at which the design becomes buildable.
People willing to do technical development and clause-by-clause code checking and to handle multi-disciplinary conflicts.

Consolidate specialist conditions from structure, plumbing, heating and electrical systems and fire protection, draw construction nodes and details, check item by item against codes on fire protection, evacuation, accessibility and energy efficiency, and complete the construction drawings and review.

Facing infrastructure and structural engineering; the focus is loads and structural calculation and materials and construction technology, and the conclusions serve engineering safety rather than building function and spatial quality.
People willing to do structural calculation and engineering analysis and to bear engineering safety responsibility.

Carry out structural selection, force analysis and calculation, design foundations and members and issue calculation books and construction drawings, and take part in construction technical proposals and acceptance.
Civil engineer (adjacent occupation)

Facing construction execution; the focus is programme, cost, quality and site safety management, the basis is the construction contract and the drawings, and design responsibility still rests with the designer.
People willing to do organisation and coordination and programme and cost control on a construction site.
Organise construction resources and work sections, prepare and track programme and cost plans, implement quality and safety measures and handle site coordination and changes.
Construction manager (adjacent occupation)
Facing interior space; the focus is space, surfaces, materials, furnishing and lighting, and the concern is the indoor experience rather than the building itself and structural safety.
People willing to do interior space, materials, furniture and light fitting selection.

Produce interior layouts and surface designs to use requirements, select materials, furniture and light fittings, issue interior construction drawings and visualisations and support site implementation.

The following five steps are an editorial suggestion; the AIA responsible use guide supports the directions of professional review, institutional policy and data protection, but it is not a Chinese statutory mandatory process and does not prove that tool output is necessarily compliant.

First confirm the design stage, use and code basis, the drawing and model and review traceability standards, and the confidentiality requirements for client and project data, and make clear which judgements must be borne by the registered architect personally.

Limit the tool to the permitted steps, such as scheme sketching and visualisation generation, drawing and model organisation and annotation, code and standard searching, and batch estimating of quantities and energy consumption, and do not let it directly produce design documents that can be issued or built, or conclusions on construction methods.

The architect checks the tool output against site conditions, specialist conditions and the current codes, reviews the dimensions, levels, materials, methods and code clauses, and records the human judgement and the reasons for the changes.

Fill in drawing and model versions, review records and design changes truthfully as required by the institution and the technical archive, keep the calculation books and their basis, so that design quality is verifiable and traceable, and archive and retain them as required.

The fit judgements on this page are all editorial suggestions based on the O*NET interest profile, work context and task data, and do not constitute recruitment or registration standards, a qualification examination, legal advice or a health or psychological diagnosis; registration and practice requirements are governed by the Regulations on Registered Architects of the People's Republic of China and the official information of the housing and urban-rural development authorities and the registered architects administration committees.

This occupation is Architect (O*NET 17-1011.00), with the interest code RCA (Realistic, Conventional, Artistic). Fit should be judged by observable behaviour: whether the person can invest over the long term in drawing development, code checking and specialist integration (48% consider precision or accuracy extremely important and 39% very important), whether the person can move projects forward in client communication and multi-disciplinary coordination (70% consider teamwork extremely important, 61% have face-to-face discussions every day and 83% have telephone conversations every day), and whether the person can adapt to long hours at a desk and a longer working week (65% sit continuously or almost continuously, 57% work more than 40 hours per week and 78% have a regular fixed schedule).
Landscape architect
Suited to people willing to design the site, outdoor space, landscape and ecology together.

The focus is the site, outdoor space, landscape and municipal interfaces, and the concern is the outdoor environment, ecology and public space quality; if the person wants the building itself, structural safety and internal function, they need to understand the boundary between landscape and architecture and how the two coordinate.
Civil engineer
Suited to people willing to do structural calculation and engineering analysis and to bear engineering safety responsibility.

The focus is loads and structural calculation and materials and construction technology, and the conclusions serve engineering safety; the basis differs from architectural design, which aims at function, space and form, and structural calculation ability must be built up.
Architectural and engineering manager
Suited to people willing to do project organisation and team, programme and cost management.

The focus is project organisation, resources, programme, cost and people management, and technical judgement is no longer the individual's main output; contract, budget and team management ability must be built up.
Construction manager
Suited to people willing to do organisation and coordination and programme and cost control on a construction site.

The focus is construction organisation, site safety, quality, programme and cost, and the basis is the construction contract and drawings; design responsibility still rests with the designer and the responsibility system differs.
Interior designer
Suited to people willing to do interior space, materials, furnishing and lighting design.

The focus is the indoor experience, surfaces, materials, furniture and light fittings, and the building itself and its structure are generally not altered; the scope and responsibility differ from architectural design.
Urban and regional planner
Suited to people willing to work on land use, transport, public policy and plan preparation.

The focus is land use, transport, public facilities and policy analysis at the urban and regional scale, and the output is planning documents and policy advice rather than the design documents of a single building.

Reliability comes from observable behaviour: whether the person can complete and review drawings, calculations and design records to the codes, whether the person states the basis and limitations truthfully when data is insufficient or a scheme is questioned, and whether the person can keep producing reviewable design documents over the long term.

Being introverted is not an obstacle; design work involves a great deal of independent development, drafting and review time, but client communication, scheme presentation and multi-disciplinary coordination require active expression (61% have face-to-face discussions every day, 83% have telephone conversations every day, 100% use email every day and 27% consider dealing with external customers or the public extremely important).

paragraphs: The risk list cannot replace the current Regulations on Registered Architects, the detailed rules, engineering standards and institutional review systems. An unregistered person must not practise in the name of a registered architect; ordinary design support does not thereby become unlawful across the board. Practising beyond scope, signing on someone's behalf or a design quality accident are handled through the competent procedures.

Four categories of risk are mainly checked: the registered name, grade and unit scope; design quality and codes; drawing versions, changes and review records; and site safety and project data confidentiality. Scheme design emphasises requirements and multi-party coordination, construction drawings emphasise closure of the disciplines and review, and upgrading emphasises existing conditions and technical conditions; the consequences are a conditional editorial analysis, not an accident rate.

Evidence scope: O*NET 17-1011.00 provides tasks and work context (48% consider precision or accuracy extremely important and 39% very important; 22% consider the consequences very serious when errors are hard to correct, 35% serious and 26% somewhat serious; 57% work more than 40 hours per week and 78% have a regular fixed schedule; 65% sit continuously or almost continuously; 17% face conflict situations every day, 22% consider competition extremely intense and 48% highly competitive; 61% have face-to-face discussions every day, 83% have telephone conversations every day and 100% use email every day). The mainland China side provides the provisions of the Regulations on Registered Architects of the People's Republic of China and the Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Regulations on Registered Architects of the People's Republic of China on examination, registration, practice, sealing and obligations. The risk scenarios, consequences and responses are an editorial summary; this page does not include accident rates or penalty amounts that are not supported by sources. The AIA guide is only industry advice on responsible use and is not presented as Chinese mandatory law.
People who practise in the name of a registered architect and hold the sealing authority

Practising in the name of a registered architect without registration, lending one's name or exceeding scope must be handled according to the specific unlawful act; unregistered support work must not be conflated with the revocation of a qualified person's certificate.

Before taking on registered practice, check one's own grade, the unit's qualification and the project scope; main design documents for projects of the stipulated scale are sealed by the registered architect in charge of the design, and review records are kept. Support staff assist under guidance and authorisation and must not use the registered name or sign on someone's behalf.
Practising in the name of a registered architect without registration, using another person's name to seal, or a registered person taking on a project beyond their grade or the unit's business scope.
Posts for design quality and code checking

Detailing, fire resistance and evacuation measures that do not meet engineering construction standards, or specialist conditions that are not closed, may lead to design defects and construction hazards or even a major liability accident.

Check fire compartments, evacuation, accessibility and energy efficiency item by item against the engineering construction standards, close the specialist conditions for structure and plumbing, heating and electrical systems, explain the basis for the construction methods and material selection, and keep the calculation and code checking records.
Taking code clauses out of context or relying on an outdated version, or issuing drawings before the specialist conditions are confirmed.
Posts for drawing, model and design change management
Drawing and model versions that are out of control, or design changes that leave no record, lead to construction rework, cost disputes and unclear responsibility.

Editorial suggestion: manage the released versions of drawings and models and keep review records. Article 32 of the Detailed Rules: modification of an already sealed document is in principle carried out by the original registered architect; in special circumstances the legal representative of the design unit may in writing commission another registered architect who meets the conditions to modify and seal it and be responsible for the modified part, and a record alone is not enough to allow the drawing to be changed.
Using an uncontrolled version of the drawings on site, or confirming changes only verbally or in instant messaging without keeping a record.
Posts for site observation and travel
Site observation and travel may involve injuries such as workplace accidents, traffic accidents and falling objects.

Wear personal protective equipment and follow site safety management as required by the construction site, implement travel and insurance arrangements, and suspend observation and report when safety hazards exist.
Entering a construction site without protective equipment, or carrying out observation at locations and times that are not safe.
Posts involving client, tender and cost information
This may infringe the client's trade secrets and lead to compliance disputes and loss of trust.

Keep confidential, in accordance with the law, the secrets of units and individuals learned in practice; the editorial suggestion is to limit the scope of use by content, client agreement and institutional authorisation. Where client or institutional confidential data is involved, the AIA guide advises against sending it to AI systems that have not been reviewed; public, authorised data and confidential material must be checked separately.
Sending out or using client requirements, tender prices, cost and technical schemes for unrelated projects.
Posts under schedule and tender pressure
This may lead to issuing drawings without review, simplified methods or omitted code checking, reducing the quality of the design documents.

Complete checking, review and approval under the institutional review system and keep records, do not exempt code checking and sealing procedures under schedule or tender pressure, and where necessary apply through the proper procedure to adjust the plan.
Skipping review or arbitrarily simplifying construction methods on grounds of schedule or tender.

items.title: How do architect entry posts and initial tasks compare?

values: Education and preparation

Every US state and the District of Columbia requires architects to be licensed, usually through architectural education, supervised paid internship and a qualification examination; the internship is generally about 3 years and some student experience may count towards it. The related work experience of none in the BLS entry-level table does not exempt a person from the licensing internship. The O*NET education responses of 43% master's, 39% bachelor's and 13% post-bachelor certificate are a distribution of responses about the education needed for new entrants and cannot replace state statutory requirements.

The current Regulations on Registered Architects were amended again on January 30, 2026, taking effect from March 20; this amendment concerns the wording of sanctions and the review and litigation procedures for refusal and revocation of registration, and does not change the eligibility conditions in Articles 8 and 9. There are five first class paths: a master's degree or above in architecture, or a doctoral degree in engineering in a closely related field, plus 2 years of related practice; a bachelor's degree in architecture or a master's degree in engineering in a closely related field plus 3 years; a bachelor's degree in architecture plus 5 years, or a bachelor's degree in a closely related field plus 7 years; senior engineer plus 3 years, or engineer plus 5 years; and other applicants who must have outstanding design achievements recognised by the national administration committee. Routes 3 to 5 also require a bachelor's degree. There are five second class paths: a bachelor's degree or above in architecture or a closely related field plus 2 years; a college diploma or above in architectural design technology or a closely related field plus 3 years; a 4-year secondary diploma in architectural design technology plus 5 years; a secondary diploma in a closely related field plus 7 years; and assistant engineer or above plus 3 years. The field correspondence, practice training and material must be checked against the examination notice for the year, and first class also requires at least 700 professional practice units.
Education, practice and work samples are checked separately, and a degree or software proficiency does not equal registration authority.
Registration and practice boundaries

In mainland China, a distinction must be drawn between design support posts and registered practice: an unregistered person may assist with drafting, document organisation and design in a design unit under the guidance and review of the person in charge, but must not practise in the name of a registered architect or sign on their behalf. A registered architect must register with a unit that holds an engineering design qualification, and the unit accepts commissions and charges uniformly; first class practice is not limited by project scale or complexity, second class practice is limited to stipulated small projects, and the individual scope is also subject to the unit's business scope. The main design documents for projects of the stipulated scale must be signed and sealed by the registered architect in charge of the design. Article 27 of the Detailed Rules sets out the registration of other relevant units and building engineering design activity separately: the latter must be employed by and registered with a unit that holds an engineering design qualification, and not all related practice activity is confined to design units.

A registered architect must keep secrets in accordance with the law, must not conduct business in two or more design units at the same time and must not lend their own name; specific site safety and entry material are checked against employer requirements, and no uniform criminal record certificate threshold is set.
O*NET work characteristics

The interest code for O*NET 17-1011.00 is RCA (Realistic, Conventional, Artistic); work activities are dominated by decision making and problem solving (90) and creative thinking (90), followed by drafting, laying out and specifying technical devices, parts and equipment (88), getting information (88), working with computers (88), communicating with people outside the organisation (86), and organising, planning and prioritising work (85).

The work context is characterised by high precision and by consequences when errors are hard to correct (48% consider precision or accuracy extremely important and 39% very important; 22% consider the consequences very serious when errors are hard to correct, 35% serious and 26% somewhat serious), a longer working week and a regular fixed schedule (57% more than 40 hours, 78% regular and fixed) and long hours at a desk (65% sit continuously or almost continuously); 22% consider competition extremely intense, 48% highly competitive and 22% moderately competitive.

Requirements for cooperation and external communication are high (70% consider teamwork extremely important and 22% very important; 27% consider dealing with external customers or the public extremely important and 27% very important; 61% have face-to-face discussions every day, 83% have telephone conversations every day and 100% use email every day), and decision-making freedom is mainly limited or some (35% limited freedom, 26% some freedom and 26% a great deal of freedom).
Tools and human judgement

O*NET lists 24 categories of software skills, including CAD, analysis, documentation and project management; BLS supports CADD/BIM for design. Energy consumption, daylight, evacuation simulation, standards libraries and collaborative review are tool suggestions selected per specific project, and penetration by post was not verified.
Some directions use three-dimensional scanning and existing-building survey tools; whether licensed software and a collaborative platform are provided must be checked with the institution.

Tools cannot replace design judgement: functional and spatial organisation, detailing and material selection, the choice of how to apply the codes, and design responsibility and sealing remain the architect's responsibility and must be recorded truthfully.

items.title: What do employers usually look at during recruitment?

values: Complete fictional material

Fictional material one | Chenghe Community Cultural Activity Centre, a single-storey concept exercise. The site is a 50m × 40m rectangle and the exercise setback is 5m on all four sides; the net usable indoor functional area given for this question is 600 sq m. The exercise height limit is 8.0m and the draft height is 8.6m. Surrounding daylight and terrain data are still missing and must be listed as to be verified; real planning compliance cannot be determined.

Fictional material two | The client requires an activity hall of 350 sq m, a reading room of 200 sq m and administration and service space of 100 sq m, 750 sq m in total; 150 sq m of this exceeds the 600 sq m. The meeting authorised a comparison of two options: A adjusts the activity hall to 200 sq m with everything else unchanged; B keeps the original functional areas but requires separate checks on extension land and investment, and has not been approved. The accessible entrance and the fire protection system are listed as non-removable design constraints.

Fictional material three | Sketch nodes P(0,0), Q(12,0) and R(12,16); the evacuation route is measured as the P→Q→R polyline and may not be replaced by the straight line PR; it is used only for the 25m limit given in this exercise. Drawing A01 v0.2 is missing the north arrow, A02 v0.1 is missing the height datum, and nodes D01 v0.1 are missing the waterproofing lap detail; there is no building category, occupant number or formal code clause, so real fire safety compliance cannot be claimed on the basis of the 25m figure.

Fictional material four | The budget is 240 ten-thousand yuan; the draft of 750 sq m is estimated at 4,000 yuan per sq m on the same basis defined in the question, giving 300 ten-thousand yuan. This unit price already includes the fire protection and accessibility facilities assumed in the question; taxes, off-site works and price fluctuation are not counted separately for now. The client wrote in asking whether the fire protection and accessibility items can be deleted, and the institution requires a reply of no more than 500 characters. The meeting decided to compare A and B first and have each discipline check the work; the formal construction drawings have not been approved.

Fictional material five | For node and minutes practice: the external wall insulation layer connects to the roof insulation layer, and the roof waterproofing turns up and is finished against the wall; thickness, fire resistance rating, lap length and structural conditions are not provided. List the to-be-verified items and do not enter statutory limits yourself. All of the above is invented by the author and cannot be used for permit applications, sealing or actual works.
Delivery tasks

Task one | List the 600 sq m area constraint, the height limit and the missing data, compare A and B and give a concept option; explain the entrance, activity and reading area circulation and the specialist conditions still to be verified.

Task two | Calculate the area excess, the draft height excess, the polyline evacuation distance and the budget difference; judge the exercise result against the 25m given in the question. The checklist should cover material version, input, calculation, type of basis, conclusion and items for the responsible person to confirm; distinguish teaching constraints from formal regulations.

Task three | Submit a client reply of no more than 500 characters, a draft node marked as to be verified and meeting minutes of no more than 500 characters. The fire protection and accessibility constraints set in the question must not be deleted; state that approval, specialist review and verification against the formal codes are not yet complete.
Reference calculations and deliverables

Reference calculation | 750 − 600 = 150 sq m of excess area; 8.6 − 8.0 = 0.6m of excess height; PQ + QR = 12 + 16 = 28m, which is 3m more than the 25m exercise limit. The straight line PR of 20m cannot be used as the given route length. The draft 750 × 4,000 = 300 ten-thousand yuan, which is 60 ten-thousand yuan, or 25%, more than the 240 ten-thousand yuan budget; A gives 600 × 4,000 = 240 ten-thousand yuan, meeting the budget only at the unit price defined on the same basis in the question.

Reference check | For A, confirm whether the 200 sq m activity hall meets the occupant numbers and use requirements; B still awaits land, planning and investment permits. Reduce the height to no more than the 8.0m given in the question and re-check the detailing; the evacuation route needs adjustment and must be determined by specialists according to the real category, occupant numbers and current codes, and cannot be certified by the 25m figure in this exercise. Add the A01 north arrow, the A02 height datum and the basis for the D01 waterproofing lap, unify the released version and keep the review records.

Reference reply (no more than 500 characters) | The draft functional area is 750 sq m, which exceeds the given net area of 600 sq m by 150 sq m; the height of 8.6m also exceeds the 8.0m set in the question. At 4,000 yuan per sq m in this question, the draft is estimated at 300 ten-thousand yuan, which is 60 ten-thousand yuan more than the 240 ten-thousand yuan budget. We suggest comparing option A, which adjusts the activity hall to 200 sq m: a total area of 600 sq m, estimated at 240 ten-thousand yuan on the same basis, but the occupant numbers and functional requirements must be confirmed. Option B keeps the original area and still requires verification of the extension permit and the investment. Fire protection and accessibility facilities cannot be treated as deletable items, and real compliance cannot be judged from a teaching limit. The evacuation route, nodes and specialist conditions await checking; the formal drawings can only proceed after client confirmation, specialist review and any necessary approval.

Reference node and minutes | The node shows only the principle of continuous insulation and an upstand waterproofing termination; material specification, fire resistance conditions and lap length are all listed as to be verified. Minutes: the client has not yet approved A or B; the architectural discipline re-checks the area, the height and the 28m route, the structural discipline confirms whether adjustment is feasible, the mechanical, electrical and fire protection disciplines check the systems and evacuation conditions, and cost checking reviews the estimate scope; the decision is submitted only after the data is complete and the review is finished. The minutes must be marked with the simulated date, version, responsible roles and unconfirmed items.
Scope of use

The work is only used to show readiness and method; it does not constitute a skills test, an opinion on qualification examinations or a recruitment test, nor does it represent the endorsement of any institution or the assumption of design responsibility.

Real project and client information and internal institutional documents must not be included in the work; all the exercise material is fictional and the drawings and conclusions cannot be used in actual works.

paragraphs: The current Regulations on Registered Architects were amended again on January 30, 2026, taking effect from March 20; this amendment concerns the wording of sanctions and the review and litigation procedures for refusal and revocation of registration, and does not change the eligibility conditions in Articles 8 and 9. There are five first class paths: a master's degree or above in architecture, or a doctoral degree in engineering in a closely related field, plus 2 years of related practice; a bachelor's degree in architecture or a master's degree in engineering in a closely related field plus 3 years; a bachelor's degree in architecture plus 5 years, or a bachelor's degree in a closely related field plus 7 years; senior engineer plus 3 years, or engineer plus 5 years; and other applicants who must have outstanding design achievements recognised by the national administration committee. Routes 3 to 5 also require a bachelor's degree. There are five second class paths: a bachelor's degree or above in architecture or a closely related field plus 2 years; a college diploma or above in architectural design technology or a closely related field plus 3 years; a 4-year secondary diploma in architectural design technology plus 5 years; a secondary diploma in a closely related field plus 7 years; and assistant engineer or above plus 3 years. The field correspondence, practice training and material must be checked against the examination notice for the year, and first class also requires at least 700 professional practice units.

In mainland China, a distinction must be drawn between design support posts and registered practice: an unregistered person may assist with drafting, document organisation and design in a design unit under the guidance and review of the person in charge, but must not practise in the name of a registered architect or sign on their behalf. A registered architect must register with a unit that holds an engineering design qualification, and the unit accepts commissions and charges uniformly; first class practice is not limited by project scale or complexity, second class practice is limited to stipulated small projects, and the individual scope is also subject to the unit's business scope. The main design documents for projects of the stipulated scale must be signed and sealed by the registered architect in charge of the design.

Under the detailed rules, subject examination passes are valid for 8 years for first class and 4 years for second class, registration is valid for 2 years, and renewal must be applied for 30 days before expiry; continuing education requires 40 class hours each of required and elective study in every period. The design unit bears liability for compensation for design quality losses and may seek recovery from the registered architect who signed.

Every US state and the District of Columbia requires architects to be licensed, usually through architectural education, supervised paid internship and a qualification examination; the internship is generally about 3 years and some student experience may count towards it. The related work experience of none in the BLS entry-level table does not exempt a person from the licensing internship. The O*NET education responses of 43% master's, 39% bachelor's and 13% post-bachelor certificate are a respondent distribution and cannot replace state statutory requirements.

The 2022 related sub-category of building and municipal design engineering technicians (2-02-18-01) has a relatively broad scope; this page provides a checking route and does not decide enrolment, registration or recruitment on behalf of any institution.

entries.answer: Within the commission, architects complete the scheme, the construction drawings, specialist integration and code checking and are accountable for the design documents; construction quality and site safety are the responsibility of the construction unit and the construction manager; the supervision unit is responsible for quality and schedule monitoring; structural and plumbing, heating and electrical specialist design is the responsibility of the corresponding professional engineers; interior space, materials and furnishing are the responsibility of the interior designer; the site and landscape are the responsibility of the landscape architect; land use, transport and planning policy are the responsibility of the urban and regional planner; bills of quantities and pricing are the responsibility of the cost engineer; planning permission and construction drawing and fire design review are the responsibility of the competent authorities and the review bodies. In this session the above materials were actually read on 2026-10-09; the OOH terminal returned 403 but the web body text was retrieved successfully. The entry point to the complete AIA survey report is now the 2026 specification report and requires a form, so the complete 2025 methodology was not obtained and no sampling or survey period is invented; the three-page guide has been read. The Shanghai notice was checked for extensions this round, and not all pilot duties were checked.

Insufficient evidence: precise occupational or city wages for Chinese architects, nationwide employment projections, AI adoption rates and wage-employment causality and the predictive validity of personality remain unobtained; the AIA2025 survey summary is only a historical industry reference, and the complete methodology and subsequent same-basis changes were not checked. The O*NET current reference period is 2025/2025—2035, and EP4.3%, OOH4% and their 3%—4% label are checked separately. FAQs outside the scope still contain old O*NET projections and broad AI gap statements, which are kept unchanged this round under authorisation with the conflict reported; historical facts that have no current nine-module consumer are retained. Exercises, works and the seven-day plan are outside the scope of revision and acceptance this round.

facts.display_value: An architect is responsible for architectural scheme and construction drawing design and specialist integration and signs design documents under the Regulations; a landscape architect is responsible for site and landscape planning and design, a naval architect and marine engineer for ships and offshore structures, a civil engineer for structural calculation and civil engineering design, and construction management and cost posts for construction organisation and pricing; when choosing a direction, the output, responsibility and scope of practice should each be checked separately.
facts.measure: Boundaries with adjacent occupations

facts.display_value: Before entering this occupation, employer requirements, post training and statutory registered practice qualification should be checked separately: the O*NET education information on the US side shows that most practitioners hold a master's or bachelor's degree and need to complete an internship and an examination to obtain a state licence; on the mainland China side, working on building design requires obtaining first or second class registered architect qualification under the Regulations on Registered Architects of the People's Republic of China, and examination application and registration have education and professional practice year requirements.
facts.measure: Entry and qualification boundaries

facts.display_value: Observable fit signals include: being able to find specific problems around design drawings and spatial function, complete architectural schemes and construction drawings to the codes and integrate the disciplines, write design notes and review records clearly, and stop, record and escalate when codes conflict, the budget is constrained or the work exceeds the scope of practice, rather than relying on personality labels.
facts.measure: Fit signals
Official occupation code

facts.display_value: The official task chain of an architect includes: preparing scale drawings or architectural design schemes and integrating engineering elements; planning and designing buildings to codes on environment and safety and so on; communicating functional and spatial requirements with clients; preparing construction contract documents and final construction drawings; visiting sites regularly to observe whether construction matches the drawings; and carrying out design for green building and existing building upgrading. Actual delivery should leave records of tasks, review, anomalies and double-checking.
facts.measure: Core workflow
